title: SRT to VTT Converter (Free, In Your Browser)
metaDescription: Convert SRT subtitles to WebVTT for free. Paste the text or drop a .srt file: it's converted in your browser and never uploaded.
intro: Drop an .srt file or paste its text to get a WebVTT (.vtt) file. The conversion runs in your browser, so the file never leaves your device.
summary: Turn .srt subtitles into WebVTT, in your browser, without uploading.

formats.heading: SRT
paragraphs: SubRip (.srt) is the most common subtitle file. Each cue has a number, a start and an end time written like 00:00:01,000, and one or more lines of text.

formats.heading: WebVTT
paragraphs: WebVTT (.vtt) is the subtitle format of web video players. The file starts with a WEBVTT line, times use a dot before the milliseconds (00:00:01.000), and cue numbers are optional.

formats.heading: What the converter changes
paragraphs: It adds the WEBVTT header, writes the times with a dot, and drops the cue numbers. The text of each cue, line breaks included, stays as it was.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The file is read and converted in your browser, and the .vtt file is created on your device.

faq.question: Are line breaks and special characters kept?
faq.answer: Yes. Each cue keeps its lines exactly as written, and the output is UTF-8.

faq.question: Why was my file rejected?
faq.answer: Each cue needs a timing line such as 00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:02,500. The error message names the first cue that doesn't have one, so you can fix it and try again.

cta.heading: Need the captions inside the video?
cta.text: Supertitle transcribes your video and exports an MP4 with the captions burned in, visible on every platform.
